tagBoundaryRuling: TAG BOUNDARY, ruled for this door. A non-word built from the row's letters at the wrong positions is still the vr13-not-a-word mistake. That covers all three build methods: right first piece with a nearby wrong pair, a nearby wrong pair then the right second piece, and one letter slipped. Reasons: (1) The entry that owns an option is the one whose hint would have stopped the child. A non-word is caught by 'Say your finished word out loud', which comes after any placement error. A real word built at the wrong positions passes that check and only the position hint catches it, so wrong-pieces keeps real-word results. (2) The opposite ruling empties the tag on this door. Every non-word made from row letters would become wrong-pieces, leaving not-a-word only letters off the row (refused as BRAM in pass 1) or re-orderings of the right pieces (refused for the anagram cue in round 1). (3) The signed house example DRAP takes its A from the third letter of DRAGON, so it is this same case. Consequence: an execution under this tag may say where its letters came from, and must, because that is what makes each letter checkable on the row. The mistake it names stays not hearing the result. This supersedes the house-form half of my first-pass DREL refusal; the BRAM refusal stands, because its A is on neither word. LIMIT of the ruling: it holds only for a non-word that 'say it aloud' actually catches. A value that sounds like a real word when read aloud does not get this tag.
